ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, R(s) enters the first summing point from the left, and the output C(s) is fed back through the lower unit feedback to the negative terminal of this summing point, so the error signal is E(s). E(s) first passes through the compensator G_C(s), and then is added at the second summing point with the disturbance D(s) entering from above; the output of this summing point then enters the controlled object G_P(s), and finally C(s) is obtained. Then reason: Only examine the steady-state error caused by the disturbance, and let R(s)=0. From the structure it can be written as C(s)=G_P(s)[G_C(s)E(s)+D(s)], and E(s)=R(s)-C(s)=-C(s). Therefore C(s)[1+G_C(s)G_P(s)]=G_P(s)D(s), so E(s)/D(s)=-G_P(s)/(1+G_C(s)G_P(s)). The disturbance is a unit step, D(s)=1/s. By the final value theorem, e_ss=lim_{s->0}sE(s)=-G_P(0)/(1+G_C(0)G_P(0)). Here G_P(0)=2.2, G_C(0)=K, therefore |e_ss|=2.2/(1+2.2K). It is required that |e_ss|<=0.1, then 2.2/(1+2.2K)<=0.1, solving gives K>=(22-1)/2.2=9.54545.... Given to two decimal places according to the standard answer of the problem, it is 9.54.

Apply the final value theorem for a unit-step disturbance: e_ss=lim_{s->0} s[E(s)] = -G_P(0)/(1+G_C(0)G_P(0)). ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, R(s) enters the first summing point from the left, and the output C(s) is fed back through the lower unit feedback to the negative terminal of this summing point, so the error signal is E(s). E(s) first passes through the compensator G_C(s), and then is added at the second summing point with the disturbance D(s) entering from above; the output of this summing point then enters the controlled object G_P(s), and finally C(s) is obtained.

Then reason: Only examine the steady-state error caused by the disturbance, and let R(s)=0. From the structure it can be written as C(s)=G_P(s)[G_C(s)E(s)+D(s)], and E(s)=R(s)-C(s)=-C(s). Therefore C(s)[1+G_C(s)G_P(s)]=G_P(s)D(s), so E(s)/D(s)=-G_P(s)/(1+G_C(s)G_P(s)).

The disturbance is a unit step, D(s)=1/s. By the final value theorem, e_ss=lim_{s->0}sE(s)=-G_P(0)/(1+G_C(0)G_P(0)). Here G_P(0)=2.2, G_C(0)=K, therefore |e_ss|=2.2/(1+2.2K). It is required that |e_ss|<=0.1, then 2.2/(1+2.2K)<=0.1, solving gives K>=(22-1)/2.2=9.54545.... Given to two decimal places according to the standard answer of the problem, it is 9.54.
